units.name: wichita group
units.lithology: The Wichita group consists of sandstone, shale, and limestone, and in the lower part contains sequences of gray and red shale, sandstone, and coal.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: cisco group
units.lithology: includes strata of Late Pennsylvanian (Virgilian) and Early Permian (Wolfcampian) ages and incorporates several boundary defined formations consisting of complexly alternating terrigenous clastic and limestone units
units.bounds_note: It overlies the carbonate and mudstone Canyon Group and grades upward into Wolfcampian redbed, carbonate, and evaporite facies of the Wichita-Albany and Clear Fork groups.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: canyon group
units.lithology: The Canyon sedimentary sequence is crudely cyclical. The “Palo Pinto”,¹ Staff, Winchell, Ranger, and Home Creek Limestones are interbedded with the Wolf Mountain, Placid and Colony Creek Shales.
units.bounds_note: The base of the Canyon Group is marked by the base of the Palo Pinto Limestone, and the group thickens progressively from its type area northeastward into the Fort Worth Basin.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: palo pinto formation
units.lithology: The limestone ledges of the Palo Pinto, Graford, Brad, and Caddo Creek formations are unevenly bedded, impure, and break in many places into small, rough-surfaced chips
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: strawn group
units.lithology: This part of the Strawn consists chiefly of gray to greenish-gray clayey shale, which weathers to bright-red clayey soil, and contains considerable plant material, mostly prints of stems and leaves.
units.bounds_note: The unit spans from the top of the Smithwick shale of the Bend group up to the base of the Brownwood shale member of the Graford formation of the Canyon group, with the upper third marked by conglomeratic channel-fill deposits cutting into underlying shale.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: caddo limestone
units.lithology: a *carbonate* unit of *Atokan* age occurring within the *Fort Worth Basin*
units.bounds_note: The Texas Railroad Commission designated the top of the Bend Conglomerate as the base of the Caddo Limestone, though faunal and age relationships suggest it should instead be included within the Bend Conglomerate.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: atoka group
units.lithology: the terms “Bend Conglomerates” and “Atoka Group” are essentially synonymous, and can be used interchangeably
units.bounds_note: The base of the overlying Strawn Group is used as the top of the Atoka, marking a major eustatic flooding surface; the Caddo Limestone is included within the Atoka Group at its top.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: bend conglomerate
units.lithology: The Bend Conglomerate is an interval of the Atoka group deposited in the Fort Worth Basin during the Middle Pennsylvanian. It consists of many genetic sequences characterized by Conglomerate depositions
units.bounds_note: The Bend begins at the Caddo Formation and ends at the Vineyard Formation, with erosional surfaces between formations defining the reservoirs; per Railroad Commission of Texas, it spans from the base of the Caddo Limestone to the top of the Marble Falls Limestone.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: smithwick shale
units.lithology: The Smithwick Shale in this field consists of about 200 feet of rather dense, carbonaceous, fissile shale with sand lentils.
units.bounds_note: Below the shale lies about 200 feet of limestone (the 'Caddo lime'/'Breckenridge lime'/'False black lime'), which becomes shaley toward its lower portion; below that is 100 feet of shale also belonging to the Smithwick.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: marble falls limestone
units.lithology: The formation consists of dark-gray and black, hard, fossiliferous limestones, interbedded with thinner layers of black, highly carbonaceous, splintery shale.
units.bounds_note: Overlies the Barnett formation conformably at the base of the Smithwick shale forms its top; thickness ranges from about 400 feet in the west to 1000+ feet east of Mineral Wells.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: barnett shale
units.lithology: The Barnett Shale consists of shale and limestone. The shale properties are dense, organic-rich, soft, thin-bedded, petroliferous, and fossiliferous. The limestone properties are hard, black, finely crystalline, petroliferous, and fossiliferous.
units.bounds_note: Karst collapse features extend vertically through the Barnett, Marble Falls, and Atoka strata, connecting the Barnett to overlying reservoirs as migration pathways.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: mississippian limestone
units.lithology: possibly in some places on white or pinkish-white Mississippian limestone
units.bounds_note: The Barnett formation lies unconformably upon the Ellenburger limestone, or possibly in places on the Mississippian limestone, indicating the Mississippian limestone underlies the Barnett unconformably in some areas.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment

units.name: ellenburger group
units.lithology: It is light gray or white, massively bedded, hard, crystalline, and dolomitic.
units.bounds_note: The Ellenburger limestone underlies the Carboniferous strata of Palo Pinto County; the Barnett formation lies unconformably upon it.
units.evidence: verbatim quote verified against the cited segment
